newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish quiet day lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish quiet day lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended lower as buyers remained scarce ahead of key testimony on the U.S. economy Tuesday and Wednesday.
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan will give semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony before Congress beginning Tuesday and will wrap up on Wednesday.
Meantime, debt futures sagged amid the notion Greenspan could make comments about inflation vigilance.
"We're just nervous about Greenspan," a Treasury bond futures trader said.
The testimony begins Tuesday at 1300 CDT/1800 GMT.
The trader said that quiet, jittery trade would likely prevail until Greenspan's comments begin.
"Let's face it: tomorrow is going to be like this until one-o'clock Chicago time."
September T-bonds slipped to 113-27/32, but support at 113-24/32 and 113-13/32 was untouched. One trader noted resistance at 114-8/32, just above the 114-5/32 session high.

Minor technical weakness also weighed on September, after last week's rejection of the seven-month high at 115-2/32. Friday's subsuquent losses were a confirmation of Thursday's reversal from that peak, some said.
Some technicians said September could be forming a top, but others said a run at the 6.50-percent yield equivalent -- roughly 114-20/32 -- was likely.
The short end was frozen in a tight range Monday, hardly moving ahead of Humphrey-Hawkins testimony Tuesday. December Eurodollars had a one-tick range.
Support in December was pegged at 94.00 and 93.98.
At the close, September T-bonds were down 6/32 at 114-00, 10-year notes were down 4/32 at 109-14/32, and December Eurodollars were down 0.010 basis points at 94.045.
